newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - August 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - August 18.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Monday: IRISH TIMES - A new commission on the points system will start work next month with the task of comprehensively reviewing the 21-year old procedures under which second-level students gain entry to universities and colleges. - A man has been remanded in custody at Mountjoy Prison on charges relating to the death of a married couple in Roscommon. - Ireland's largest union, SIPTU, is to ask the government to implement the income tax cuts promised for the next two years because of higher-than-expected tax revenues. - Fruit of the Loom has dismissed claims that hundreds of jobs at its factories in Ireland are at risk. IRISH INDEPENDENT - Six children had their lives turned upside down by the double slaying in Roscommon on Saturday. - Fruit of the Loom management last night denied planning any large scale job cuts at its Irish company and hit out at what it claimed was a smear campaign. - The Dublin stock market is expected to take a hit today after Wall Street suffered the second worst fall in its history on Friday and the London stock market saw 22 billion sterling wiped off shares on the same day. THE EXAMINER - The man charged with double murder over the weekend told police he was sorry and broke down in tears in court yesterday. - East Cork rescue services were on full alert last night following eye-witness reports of a micro-light aircraft plunging into dense woodland shortly after dark. - Tipperary hurlers created history yesterday by qualifying for the All-Ireland hurling final - six weeks after they were defeated by Clare in the Munster Final.
